prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1209; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision at an intersection. The claimant reports knee pain, is not represented by a lawyer, and gave an initial statement by phone.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and scene photos. The other driver confirms the accident happened as described, and the witness accounts match. The officer's notes say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened, so I am following up on that.

Entry 3: The claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation so far. A few old scratches on the rear bumper may predate this crash, so I am checking which damage is new.

Entry 4: Medical records show the knee treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. No earlier injury to that knee is known, but it is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.

Entry 5: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy. Nothing suggests the damage happened before coverage started.

Entry 6: Sent the repair estimate to the appraiser. It is not yet clear whether all of the damage came from this impact, so the review remains open until the appraiser reports back.
